text:
mike_support: Customer (AcmeReports) reports SSE stream returns partial events and then client hangs. Happens ~3x today, region us-east-1, model=redwood-medium-2025-q4. request id from their logs: req_ab12cd34ef. They say final token(s) never arrive, client shows spinner.

ingrid_ops: Ok — we need reproduction artifacts before escalating. Ask them for: request-id(s), full response headers, curl reproduction (with -v and --no-buffer), browser HAR or websocket trace, and a short snippet of client code. Also ask for exact timestamps (UTC) when it occurred.

mike_support: Sending repro checklist to customer now. I gave them this curl example:

curl -v --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium-2025-q4","input":"hello world","stream":true}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams" 2>&1 | tee sse_out.txt

mike_support: Told them to paste sse_out.txt and grep for any "X-Redwood-Request-Id" or server-side request id lines.

alex_k: Ask them to include the full HTTP response headers from that curl run (the -v output). If they see a header like "X-Redwood-Request-Id: <id>" we can tie to infra logs. Also ask for the client UA and network type (wifi/cellular).

jessica_q: Also request a browser HAR or the websocket trace (if they're using ws). Example minimal node ws repro: 

const WebSocket = require('ws');
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.example/v1/streams', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer REDACTED' } });
ws.on('open', () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-medium-2025-q4', input: 'hi', stream: true })));
ws.on('message', (m) => console.log(new Date().toISOString(), m));
ws.on('close', () => console.log('closed'));

jessica_q: Request they run node repro for ~30 seconds and paste stdout. If messages stop arriving but connection stays OPEN, that strongly suggests server stopped sending rather than client closed.

ingrid_ops: If they can't run code, ask them to do a curl + timestamped system time output side-by-side: e.g. run: 
( date -u +%FT%T%Z; curl -v --no-buffer ... ) 2>&1 | tee debug_$(date -u +%s).log

mike_support: Customer replied with 2 logs. They included sse_out.txt but it's truncated in Slack. They gave header: "X-Redwood-Request-Id: req_ab12cd34ef" and said stream ended with a final "event: done" missing — they only see chunked partial tokens.

alex_k: Good — next ask for server-side logs for that request id. If customer is on Dedicated/Private, they should check their ingress/proxy logs (nginx/ALB) for any 499/504 or keepalive drops. If Hosted, ask support to fetch infra trace: ingrid, can you pull proxy+runtime logs for req_ab12cd34ef between 2025-11-13T14:02:00Z and 2025-11-13T14:03:30Z?

ingrid_ops: On it. Also request a debug bundle from the customer: include their client HAR or ws trace, the curl output, the exact client code snippet, and a short note of how often it reproduces. Provide upload link for attachments. 

trace-bot: @ingrid_ops created ticket INF-4217 and attached initial customer files.

mike_support: Customer also mentioned they see partial events with repeated "data: [..]" lines and long gaps (~7-12s) between them. They suspect client-side buffering. We should suggest they run curl on a different machine/network to rule out middlebox.

alex_k: Yes — counsel to try: 1) curl from a different network, 2) curl from a different OS (mac/linux), 3) disable proxies, 4) run tcpdump -w around the request to capture packet-level timing. If packet arrival shows continuous data but the client app doesn't print, it's client buffering. If packets stop, server likely stopped sending.

jessica_q: Also ask for a short timeline: client local time when stream started, last event received, and client's perceived hang time. This helps correlate with infra metrics.

ingrid_ops: Pulled runtime logs: I see request req_ab12cd34ef accepted and tokens streamed from runtime for ~1.9s then runtime reported a downstream write error to proxy at 14:02:08Z (EPIPE). I'm uploading logs to the ticket.

mike_support: Noted — passing to eng-runtime with the logs and the customer's curl/ws outputs. Customer very grateful for the fast follow-up. :thumbsup:

alex_k: Eng-runtime, please check fallback logic and proxy write-backpressure handling. If we closed the write early, we need a regression test where runtime holds stream open while client slowly reads.

ingrid_ops: Assigned ENG-RUNTIME and pinned the ticket. If we need more from customer I'll coordinate a short joint debug session (screen share).

mike_support: Thanks everyone — keeping customer updated. :eyes:
